chapter: Central Avenue clubs, Nordskog, Sheffield and Music Town
title: Who owned and ran the Alabam, the Dunbar and the Alabam cabaret
summary: Curtis Mosby owned the Alabam cabaret but not the building; Dr. Summerville built the Dunbar, and Jack Johnson briefly ran the cabaret.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Well did [Curtis] Mosby actually own it, or did he only operate it? Somebody told me...
He owned the cabaret but he didn't own the building.
Somebody said...somebody told me that a couple of Italian brothers actually owned the Alabam...
They owned the building, or they owned the club, and he worked for them?

They owned the building. No, they didn't own the...No, they owned the...they ran the Dunbar, I think--those two. There was a colored fellow owned that Alabam building. I can't think of his name now. He's been a...no, I think he'd worked for the city a long time, and I think the Italian boys opened the Dunbar after it was built. Negro built it, you know.

Dr. Summerville, and I think they ran...ran the, uh...they mixed in there somewhere, but I know the brothers. I can't think of their name but I don't think..I..I don't remember now who they were mixed in there with. Mosby ran the Dunb...the Alabam, and Dr. Summerville built the Dunbar, but he didn't run the cabaret or nothing in there. Jack Johnson ran it for awhile. The prizefighter.
The cabaret in the Alabam. See, he ran a little nightclub in the Alabam, and Jack Johnson ran it for awhile, and then Earl Dancer ran it for awhile.
